info.title: Leap Incentives — Lookups
info.description:
Partner-facing eligibility evaluation. Three operations, each its own sub-collection under the `incentives` resource:

  * `POST /v1.1/global-connect/incentives/lookups` — first-touch.
    Creates the customer if new, upserts devices, geocodes the address,
    resolves serving utilities, and evaluates eligibility.
  * `POST /v1.1/global-connect/incentives/refreshes` — re-evaluates an
    existing customer against their already-stored devices and cached
    utilities. No new customer or device rows.
  * `POST /v1.1/global-connect/incentives/overrides` — replaces the
    customer's device set with a new one (destructively wipes the
    existing devices), then evaluates against the new set.

The legacy `POST /v1.1/global-connect/incentives` path is preserved as a deprecated alias for `/lookups` so partners on the original release keep working. New integrations should use the explicit `/lookups` sub-collection.
`partner_id` is derived server-side from the authenticated principal's `leap-partnerid` header — it is intentionally not part of any request body. Accepting it from the client would turn these endpoints into an IDOR primitive over the customer / customer_device tables.

post.description: Check which rebate programs a customer qualifies for. Send the customer's address, classification, and devices; Leap returns the total incentive amount, a per-program breakdown, and a Connect URL the customer can use to apply.

200.description: Eligibility resolved (programs may be empty if the customer matches no candidates).

post.description: Re-run eligibility for a customer you've already looked up, using their stored address and devices — no need to resend them. Use this to pick up newly launched programs or updated incentive amounts.

200.description: Eligibility re-evaluated using the customer's stored state.

post.description: Replace an existing customer's device list, then re-run eligibility. Use this when a customer's equipment has changed. The previous device set is discarded.

Forbidden.description: You do not have permission to perform this operation

NotFound.description: Address is not covered by any utility we have territory data for. This is a coverage gap, not an internal failure — the caller should not retry.

UnprocessableEntity.description: Request was syntactically valid but could not be processed (e.g., unknown device id, address could not be geocoded)

RateLimited.description: The shared per-partner rate limit for /incentives endpoints was exceeded (`error_code: RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`). Back off and retry after the number of seconds indicated by the `Retry-After` header.

BadGateway.description: Upstream dependency (geocoder) is unavailable or rate-limited

reason.description: Human-readable explanation. Safe to surface to partners; no internal identifiers.

reference_id.description: Your stable identifier for this customer. Leap uses it to recognise a returning customer, and you'll send it again on **Refresh incentives**, **Override incentives**, and when searching applications. It's scoped to you — another partner using the same value is a different customer.

customer_devices.description: One entry per installation. Each carries the catalog `device_id` and an optional `partner_device_reference` that disambiguates two installs of the same catalog device. When omitted, the server assigns `"1"`, `"2"`, ... in request order, skipping any value already supplied by the partner. The inline `details` object accepts per-installation attributes (e.g. `customer_device.purchase_price`, `customer_device.installation_date`).

eiaid.description: Optional utility override. Supply it when you already know the customer's serving utility and the address-based match is unavailable or ambiguous: Leap uses this EIA utility id to select candidate programs instead of resolving the utility from the address. On this path the address isn't geocoded, so the response omits the `geocoding` block and any stored coordinates are left as they are. A value matching no utility fails the same way an unserved address does (404 `NO_UTILITY_AT_ADDRESS`).

customer_details.description: Attributes you're supplying for the customer, keyed by requirement key (for example `customer.email`, `customer.is_homeowner`). They're stored against the customer and used when eligibility is evaluated. Omit or leave empty if you have none. Maximum 100 entries.

create_application.description: Create the Connect application records for this lookup's eligible programs, so the returned `connect_url` is a link the customer can open. Provisioning runs in the background and is normally in place within seconds. Defaults to `false`: lookup-only integrations are unaffected and no applications are created for them. No effect on billing or rate limits.

include_preview.description: Include your own unpublished partner offer in the results so you can test it before publishing. Only your own offer is ever included. Utility, state, and market programs are unaffected. Defaults to `false`.

reference_id.description: Partner's stable identifier for the customer. Must match an existing customer scoped to the authenticated `partner_id`; unknown reference IDs return 404.

customer_details.description: Optional partner-supplied per-customer attributes to upsert against the existing customer record before re-evaluation. Use this to update values like `customer.is_homeowner` without touching the device set. Empty or omitted = no attribute changes.

customer_devices.description: Optional device merge set. An entry carrying a `customer_device_id` updates that installation in place; an entry without one adds a new installation. Installations already on file that you don't list are left untouched — sending a subset never deletes the rest.

remove_customer_device_ids.description: Remove installations by `customer_device_id`. Ids that don't match a device on this customer are ignored, so retries are safe.

remove_device_references.description: Remove installations by `partner_device_reference`. Every installation with a matching reference is removed; unknown references are ignored.

reference_id.description: Partner's stable identifier for the customer. Must match an existing customer scoped to the authenticated `partner_id`; unknown reference IDs return 404.

customer_devices.description: The new device set for the customer. Every existing `customer_device` row for this customer is deleted before these are inserted — there is no merge step. The same `partner_device_reference` rules from `/lookups` apply (one entry per installation, server-assigned positional defaults when blank, uniqueness enforced within the request).

customer_details.description: Optional partner-supplied per-customer attributes to upsert against the existing customer record. Same shape as on `/lookups`. Empty or omitted = no attribute changes.

CustomerDeviceRef.description: One installation. New installations identify their catalog device with exactly one of `device_id` / `device_source_id`. On **Refresh incentives**, `customer_device_id` instead targets an installation already on file, for an in-place update.

device_id.description: Catalog `device.id`. Exactly one of `device_id` / `device_source_id` is required on new installations. Optional when `customer_device_id` targets an existing installation — and must match that installation's catalog device when supplied. Must exist in the device catalog or the request is rejected with 422 `INVALID_DEVICE_ID`.

device_source_id.description: Alternative way to address the catalog device: its numeric catalog `source_id`. Unknown values are rejected with 422 `INVALID_DEVICE_ID`. Supply exactly one of `device_id` / `device_source_id` on new installations.

customer_device_id.description: Identifies one installation — this customer, this catalog device, your device reference. Leap assigns it on the first lookup and echoes it back in `customer_devices[]`; it is stable across later lookups and refreshes, and is regenerated only by **Override incentives**, which replaces the device set. Send it on **Refresh incentives** to update that installation in place; it is rejected with 400 on lookups and overrides.

partner_device_reference.description: Partner-supplied per-installation identifier. Unique within the request. Echoed back in the response so partners can join their local records to the upserted `customer_device`. Server fills in `"1"`, `"2"`, ... in request order (skipping any value the partner already supplied) when omitted.

details.description: Partner-supplied per-installation attributes keyed by `requirement.key` (e.g. `customer_device.purchase_price`). Maximum 50 entries.

device_id.description: The catalog `device.id` resolved for this installation.

partner_device_reference.description: Server-resolved value (echoed verbatim if the partner supplied one; assigned `"1"`, `"2"`, ... otherwise).

customer_device_id.description: Leap's identifier for this installation. Store it — it's how you address that specific device on later calls.

address_line_1.description: Street address — house number and street name.

address_line_2.description: Optional secondary address line, such as an apartment, suite, or unit number.

country_code.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code. Defaults to `US`.

reference_id.description: Echoes the `reference_id` from the request — the partner's stable identifier for this customer.

customer_devices.description: Per-installation echo. One entry per request entry, with the resolved (server-filled if absent) `partner_device_reference` and the upserted `customer_device.id`.

connect_url.description: Deep link to hand the customer so they can apply: `https://connect.incentives.leap.energy/{company}/refId/{reference_id}`, where `{company}` is your registration nickname. **Omitted entirely when the lookup surfaces no eligible incentive** — there is nothing to apply for, so check that the field is present before showing a link.

program_details.description: One entry per eligible (or conditionally eligible) program. Empty when no candidate programs match the (utility, customer_classification, device_category) filter.

PartnerBranding.description: Your brand name and logo as configured on your Leap account, so a surface rendering these results can show your branding without a second call.

logo_url.description: URL to your logo, as configured on your Leap account. Null when no logo is configured.

upfront_amount.description: Always 0 in the current cut. Reserved for a future "pre-install upfront" payment kind.

install_amount.description: Sum across all eligible programs of incentives paid at install time. Maps from the engine's `up_front_total` per program.

ongoing_amount.description: Total recurring incentives across all eligible programs, **per year**.

name.description: Program name as shown to the customer. Leap sets this for utility, state, and market programs; for your own partner offer it is the offer name you configure in the portal.

operator_name.description: Name of the operating utility / agency. Currently null until the display source is wired in a follow-up.

display_name.description: Partner-branded display name for the program (PARTNER_OFFER rows only). Read from `program.metadata.display_name`. Null for non-offer programs.

logo_url.description: URL to the partner's logo (PARTNER_OFFER rows only). Read from `program.metadata.logo_url`. Null for non-offer programs.

terms_url.description: URL to the partner's terms-and-conditions page (PARTNER_OFFER rows only). Read from `program.metadata.terms_url`. Null for non-offer programs.

description.description: Free-form description shown to the customer (PARTNER_OFFER rows only). Read from `program.metadata.description`. Null for non-offer programs.

is_partner_offer.description: `true` when this entry is your own partner offer (which bundles one or more underlying programs); `false` for utility, state, and market rebate programs. Use it to separate your offer from rebates in your own UI.

covered_programs.description: The wrapped Leap-Definitions programs that evaluated eligible for this customer under this offer (PARTNER_OFFER rows only) — the programs whose value is summed into this entry's tier amounts. Always empty for non-offer entries.

program_identifier.description: Stable identifier for this program — your offer's identifier for a partner offer, or the catalog identifier (for example `PGE-ART`) otherwise. Use it to correlate the same program across lookups.

included_leap_program_ids.description: Partner offers only: identifiers of the underlying programs this offer covers for this customer. Empty for every other kind of entry.

tiers.description: The program's incentive tiers evaluated for this customer. Each tier carries its payment type, total amount, and per-device results.

tier_name.description: Display name for the tier. Non-offer programs surface their spec tier id; Partner Offer legs surface customer-facing names — "Enrollment Incentive" (up-front leg) / "Participation Incentive" (recurring leg). Partner Offers emit one tier per payment leg.

incentive_amount.description: Tier total across the devices that passed this tier's requirements; per-device outcomes are in `device_results[]`. Units follow `payment_type`: `UPFRONT` and `INSTALL` amounts are one-time, `ONGOING` amounts are per year.

device_results.description: One entry per `customer_device` evaluated for this tier. Each shows whether that install passed/failed/ignored the tier's requirements and the per-check details.

identifier.description: The wrapped Leap-Definitions program's identifier. Internal detail surfaced only in `covered_programs[]` on a Partner Offer entry — never a standalone `EligibleProgram` (raw LEAP_DEFINITIONS programs are never surfaced).

name.description: Human-readable label for the wrapped program (`program.label`).

partner_device_reference.description: Echoes the `partner_device_reference` from the request's `customer_devices[]` entry.

customer_device_id.description: The `customer_device.id` of the installation evaluated in this result.

eligibility_details.description: Per-requirement check results behind this device's tier `status` — one entry per eligibility rule evaluated.

source_program_identifier.description: On a partner offer, the program this check came from — your offer's identifier for checks on the offer itself, or the identifier of an underlying program for checks it inherits. Null on rebate programs.

primary.description: The utility resolved as serving this address — the one whose programs drive the eligibility result.

possible_utilities.description: Every utility whose service territory covers this address (including `primary`); more than one can appear where territories overlap.

IncentiveUtility.description: EIA-keyed utility identity used in incentive eligibility responses. Distinct from `common-schemas.yaml#/components/schemas/Utility`, which carries Connect's UUID-based shape with logo + connection URL.

latitude.description: Latitude of the geocoded address, in decimal degrees.

longitude.description: Longitude of the geocoded address, in decimal degrees.

formatted_address.description: The address as normalized by the geocoder.

CustomerClassification.description: The customer or site classification used to determine eligibility. `RESIDENTIAL` and `COMMERCIAL` are the long-standing values; `MULTIFAMILY` and `MANUFACTURED_HOME` exist because rebate qualification differs across single-family, multifamily, and manufactured housing.

BearerAuth.description: Your Leap API key as a Bearer token. Send it in the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>`.
